At HDR, our employee-owners are fully engaged in creating a welcoming environment where each of us is valued and respected, a place where everyone is empowered to bring their authentic selves and novel ideas to work every day. As we foster a culture of inclusion throughout our company and within our communities, we constantly ask ourselves: What is our impact on the world?

Watch Our Story:' https://www.hdrinc.com/our-story'

Each and every role throughout our organization makes a difference in our ability to change the world for the better. Read further to learn how you could help make great things possible not only in your community, but around the world.

We believe transportation is more than movement, it’s the foundation of connected, thriving communities. As part of HDR’s Transportation Business Group, you’ll help shape the systems that move people and goods safely, efficiently, and sustainably. From designing resilient highways and iconic bridges to advancing transit, passenger and freight rail, aviation, federal transportation ports and marine infrastructure, your work will directly support economic vitality, public safety, sustainable and resilient communities and quality of life. We bring together planners, engineers, architects, construction management staff, environmental, strategic communications, economists, management consultants and specialists across disciplines to solve complex mobility challenges with innovation, technical excellence, and a deep understanding of community needs. Whether you're modernizing aging infrastructure or pioneering next-generation transportation solutions, your contributions will help define the future of mobility. This isn’t just a job, it’s a chance to lead progress, drive meaningful impact, and leave a legacy of smarter, more connected transportation networks. We are all employee-owners at HDR, which is the foundation of our collaborative culture that connects employees around the world.

Primary Role:

The Applied Data Scientist – AI Enablement is a high-impact individual contributor role focused on building internal AI capabilities and removing systemic constraints that limit HDR’s ability to scale artificial intelligence across the Transportation Business Group. In the initial phase, this role is primarily internally focused, developing AI solutions, improving data and technology foundations, and identifying bottlenecks in systems, processes, and tooling. As internal capabilities mature, the role will progressively transition to client-facing AI delivery and advisory work, leveraging internally proven solutions as repeatable services.

Utilization Expectations:

• 40% Internal AI solution development
• 40% Client AI delivery and pilot engagements (as capabilities mature) (0% year 1)
• 20% Skill development and continuous learning

Primary Responsibilities:

Internal AI Capability Development:

• Design, develop, and deploy AI solutions addressing internal transportation business needs (e.g., document intelligence, predictive analytics, copilots, workflow automation).
• Build reusable AI components, data pipelines, and workflows that can be scaled for future client delivery
• Manage full model lifecycle including development, deployment, monitoring, drift detection, retraining, and inference.

Constraint & Bottleneck Identification:

• Proactively identify limitations in data availability, system integration, tooling, governance, and processes that inhibit AI adoption.
• Partner with IT, data architects, and business stakeholders to recommend scalable improvements.
• Document technical debt and architectural gaps that must be addressed before scaling AI capacity.

Collaboration & Communication:

• Collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders to translate ambiguous problems into structured AI solutions.
• Communicate AI concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.

Future Client-Facing Work:

• Support client pursuits and pilot projects using internally developed AI capabilities.
• Contribute to the evolution of repeatable AI services and offerings.

Note: This is not an exhaustive list. This role requires flexibility to perform other duties as required.

Preferred Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s degree in a closely related field or equivalent combination of education and experience.
• Experience with generative AI and modern AI services.
• Hands-on experience developing, deploying, and maintaining data and AI solutions in cloud environments (e.g., Azure, AWS, or GCP), including cloud-native data pipelines, scalable compute, and production model deployment.
• Experience managing end-to-end data science projects and model lifecycles.
• Strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills.
• Advanced Degree
• Experience designing or improving data pipelines and AI infrastructure.
• Consulting or professional services experience.
• Six Sigma or other process improvement certifications.

Required Qualifications

• A degree in a closely related field or combination of education and relevant experience
• A minimum of 3 years experience with data engineering tools and languages such as SQL, Power Query, and Pandas
• A minimum of 3 years experience with business intelligence tools such as Power BI, Tableau, Plotly, Seaborn, and Matplotlib
• A minimum of 3 years experience with data science languages such as Python and R
• Self-motivated, detail-oriented professional, ability to multitask a must
• Proficiency with MS Office including Word and Outlook
• Ability to handle confidential information
• Excellent writing and people skills
• Strong math and organizational skills
• Flexibility and ability to prioritize and handle multiple tasks and various managers in a fast-paced environment
• Excellent verbal and written communication skills including grammar, punctuation, proofreading, spelling and telephone skills
• An attitude and commitment to being an active participant of our employee-owned culture is a must
• In-depth knowledge of machine learning algorithms, statistical models, and data analytics
• Experience completing multiple data science projects

What We Believe

HDR is our company. Together, we build on each other's life experiences and perspectives to make great things possible every day. This shapes our collaborative culture, encourages organizational trust and connects us closer to the clients and communities we serve.

Our Commitment

As employee owners, we all have a role in creating an inclusive environment where each of us is welcomed, valued, respected and empowered to bring our authentic selves to work every day.

Our eight Employee Network Groups (Asian Pacific, Black, Hispanic/Latino(a), LGBTQ+, People with Disabilities, Veterans, Women, Young Professionals) help create a sense of belonging and foster a supportive environment where everyone is empowered to engage and contribute. Position Title: Data Scientist

Position Overview: We are seeking a Data Scientist to support reclassification efforts across federal job series. The incumbent will apply advanced data analysis, statistical modeling, and computational techniques to workforce data and position descriptions, ensuring alignment with classification standards and helping inform accurate, data-driven decisions.

Required Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, Human Resources Analytics, or a related field (Master’s preferred).

• Strong proficiency in programming languages such as Python or R.

• Experience with natural language processing (NLP), machine learning, and data visualization.

• Knowledge of SQL and database management.

• Ability to interpret and present complex data clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.

• Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.

Key Responsibilities:

• Collect, clean, and analyze large datasets related to position descriptions, job duties, and workforce information.

• Use statistical methods, natural language processing (NLP), and machine learning techniques to identify trends, patterns, and commonalities across job roles.

• Conduct text analytics on position descriptions to map tasks, skills, and responsibilities to appropriate job series and grade levels.

• Collaborate with human resources professionals, subject matter experts, and leadership to validate data-driven findings.

• Develop dashboards, visualizations, and reports to communicate insights in a clear and actionable manner.

• Ensure consistency, accuracy, and compliance with federal classification policies and standards.

• Provide recommendations to leadership on job reclassification and series alignment based on data analysis.

• Stay current with emerging trends in workforce analytics, HR technology, and data science.

Desired Skills:

• Familiarity with federal job classification standards and Office of Personnel Management (OPM) guidance.

• Experience working with workforce or HR-related data.

• Knowledge of cloud computing environments and big data tools.

• Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with cross-functional teams.

Impact: This position plays a key role in ensuring federal positions are accurately classified, improving workforce alignment, and enabling data-driven decision-making to support organizational goals.

What are Trust Fund Positions?

Trust Fund positions are unique to the Smithsonian. They are paid for from a variety of sources, including the Smithsonian endowment, revenue from our business activities, donations, grants and contracts. Trust employees are not part of the civil service, nor does trust fund employment lead to Federal status. The salary ranges for trust positions are generally the same as for federal positions and in many cases trust and federal employees work side by side. Trust employees have their own benefit program, which may include Health, Dental & Vision Insurance, Life Insurance, Transit/Commuter Benefits, Accidental Death and Dismemberment Insurance, Annual and Sick Leave, Family Friendly Leave, 403b Retirement Plan, Discounts for Smithsonian Memberships, Museum Stores and Restaurants, Credit Union, Smithsonian Early Enrichment Center (Child Care), Flexible Spending Account (Health & Dependent Care).
Conditions of Employment

• Pass Pre-employment Background Check and Subsequent Background Investigation for position designated.

• Complete a Probationary Period.

• Maintain a Bank Account for Direct Deposit/Electronic Transfer.

• The position is open to all candidates eligible to work in the United States. Proof of eligibility to work in U.S. is not required to apply.

• Applicants must meet all qualification and eligibility requirements within 30 days of the closing date of this announcement.

OVERVIEW
This position is located in Washington, DC, within the Forest Global Earth Observatory (ForestGEO), Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute (STRI), under the Office of the Under Secretary for Science and Research at the Smithsonian Institution (SI).

STRI provides a global platform for research on tropical forests and marine ecosystems, biodiversity, and human well-being.

The ForestGEO program is a global network of scientists and forest research sites dedicated to advancing the long-term study of the world's forests.

The GEO-TREES initiative builds on this network to improve the accuracy and verification of global forest carbon estimates through collaboration among forest research sites worldwide. The Data Scientist supports the Forest Global Earth Observatory (ForestGEO) and GEO-TREES programs as a liaison between site-based data collection and the development of analytical data products.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Data Management, Scientific Analysis, and Software Programming (50%)

• Performs data-management, computational, and bioinformatics assignments supporting research in tropical biology, ecology, and forestry.

• Develops, implements, modifies, and maintains data-processing pipelines used to process plot-based tree inventory and related ecological data and to derive estimates such as forest woody biomass density.

• Evaluates the performance of existing data-processing pipelines and recommends modifications or improvements based on data characteristics, analytical requirements, user needs, and experience working with ForestGEO and GEO-TREES site teams.

• Develops and modifies computational procedures for analysis of ForestGEO and GEO-TREES scientific data using established data-science principles, methods, and practices.

• Processes, validates, organizes, and manages tree inventory, Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS), Airborne Laser Scanning (ALS), and Terrestrial Laser Scanning (TLS) data for scientific analysis and long-term storage.

• Supports the archiving and long-term management of scientific datasets to ensure appropriate organization, documentation, accessibility, and usability.

• Develops and maintains data-management solutions and informatics workflows for data acquisition, formatting, validation, processing, analysis, use, and storage.

• Implements established data standards and contributes to the development and modification of data structures and architectures appropriate to assigned projects.

• Writes, tests, documents, troubleshoots, and maintains computer code used in data-processing and analytical workflows.

• Uses programming languages and tools such as R, Python, SQL, Git, GitHub, GIS applications, and related scientific and data-management software.

• Identifies data-quality problems, inconsistencies, missing values, formatting issues, and other anomalies and determines appropriate methods for correcting or documenting them.

• Works with researchers and other technical personnel to ensure that processed data and analyticalproducts meet established scientific and program requirements.

Requirements Gathering and Technical Support (25%)

• Works closely with researchers and program personnel to identify data-processing, analytical, software, and data-management requirements for assigned scientific projects.

• Conducts technical analyses of available methods and alternatives and recommends appropriate software tools, workflows, calculations, and analytical approaches.

• Assists researchers in translating scientific requirements into practical data-processing and

• computational solutions.

• Evaluates existing workflows and recommends modifications when established approaches do not fully address the characteristics of the data or requirements of an assigned project.

• Coordinates with site representatives concerning timelines and technical requirements for acquisition and submission of plot inventory, TLS, ALS, GNSS, and related scientific data.

• Reviews submitted data to determine whether established ForestGEO and GEO-TREES formatting, documentation, and data-quality requirements have been met.

• Works with site personnel to resolve routine and moderately complex data-submission and data-quality problems.

• Coordinates with the Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) and other appropriate technical staff to ensure assigned development activities follow applicable systems-development, documentation, version-control, security, and software-development practices.

• Prepares technical documentation describing data-processing workflows, code, data structures, analytical procedures, and related methods.

• Assists in testing new or modified software tools, workflows, and procedures prior to implementation.

Training and Collaboration (25%)

• Develops and provides formal and informal training to researchers, site personnel, and program partners concerning ForestGEO and GEO-TREES data systems, data-management procedures, formatting requirements, data-processing workflows, and related tools.

• Serves as a technical point of contact for tree-inventory teams and other users at assigned ForestGEO and GEO-TREES sites.

• Provides advice, training, troubleshooting assistance, and technical support concerning data collection, formatting, cleaning, validation, processing, documentation, and submission.

• Explains data standards, analytical procedures, software requirements, and data-management practices to researchers and partners with varying levels of technical expertise.

• Collaborates with scientists, data managers, programmers, and other personnel to identify and resolve data-management and processing problems.

• Participates in meetings, working groups, and collaborative activities involving ForestGEO, GEO-TREES, Smithsonian staff, and domestic and international research partners.

• Shares information concerning lessons learned, recurring data problems, workflow improvements, and effective data-management practices with program staff and partners.

Performs other duties as assigned.

QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS
Education and Experience:

• Professional knowledge of and skill in applying a wide range of data-science principles, concepts, methods, and practices sufficient to perform difficult data-management, processing, computational, and analytical assignments involving ecological and forestry data.

• Knowledge of data acquisition, data cleaning, validation, transformation, integration, storage, analysis, visualization, documentation, and reproducible computational workflows.

• Knowledge of computational and data-management methods is required to develop, modify, implement, and maintain processing pipelines for tree inventory, GNSS, ALS, TLS, spatial, and related scientific datasets.

• Knowledge of programming concepts and skill in applying programming languages and analytical tools such as R, Python, SQL, Git, GitHub, and related software to manipulate, process, analyze, and manage scientific data.

• Knowledge of algorithm development, software testing, version control, debugging, documentation, deployment, and maintenance practices is required to support scientific applications and data-processing workflows.

• Knowledge of spatial-data concepts, common spatial-data formats, and GIS software is required to process and evaluate geospatial information associated with ForestGEO and GEO-TREES projects.

• Knowledge of the scientific concepts associated with ecology, tropical biology, forestry, or related environmental sciences sufficient to understand data characteristics, research requirements, analytical objectives, and the relationships among data variables.

• Knowledge to select and modify appropriate data-processing and analytical methods; identify and resolve data-quality problems; evaluate alternative computational approaches; interpret results; develop recommendations; and prepare technical documentation and analytical products.

• Skill adapting or modifying established data-science techniques and procedures to address differences in data structure, quality, collection methods, analytical requirements, or site-specific circumstances.

Position: Graph Data Scientist

Location: Remote, with occasional site visits to PRAC locations as required

Work Environment: Remote

Clearance Required: Public Trust (HSPD-12)

Status: Contingent Upon Contract Award

Salary Range: $125,000 - $165,000 per year

Knowesis, Inc. is seeking an experienced Graph Data Scientist to support the Pandemic Response Accountability Committee (PRAC) by developing and applying advanced graph-based analytic techniques to detect fraud, waste, abuse, and mismanagement across federal programs. The PRAC delivers data-driven oversight of pandemic relief and OBBBA Act funds and works closely with federal Offices of Inspectors General (OIGs) and federal law enforcement to ensure that covered funds are used appropriately and not subject to fraud or misuse.

The Graph Data Scientist will play a critical role within the PRAC Analytics Center, applying graph theory, network science, and machine learning to uncover hidden relationships, detect complex fraud schemes, and support investigative case development. This position will contribute to PRAC's advanced analytic support, investigative intelligence, and capability development efforts by building graph models, knowledge graphs, link analysis products, and graph-based fraud detection tools.

The PRAC analytic platform operates in a cloud-based environment using tools such as Azure Databricks, Microsoft SQL Server, Microsoft Power BI, and neo4j, along with other advanced technologies to analyze and visualize public, non-public, and commercially available data. The Graph Data Scientist will work within agile sprints and Integrated Project Teams (IPTs), collaborating with PRAC stakeholders, OIG partners, and law enforcement to deliver high-quality analytic outputs that support oversight, investigative support, and continuous capability enhancement. The role requires strong technical expertise, analytic rigor, and the ability to translate complex graph-based insights into clear, actionable intelligence for diverse stakeholders.

The Job Duties and Responsibilities include but are not limited to the following:
• Develop graph-based analytic rules and models to detect fraud, waste, abuse, and mismanagement across multi-agency and multi-program datasets.
• Apply advanced graph theory concepts-including network topology, centrality measures, community detection, and shortest-path algorithms-to identify hidden relationships and emerging fraud schemes.
• Use Neo4j (or similar graph databases) and fluently write Cypher queries to build, test, and optimize graph models and knowledge graphs supporting PRAC analytic use cases.
• Conduct exploratory data analysis and data profiling on public and non-public datasets to prepare graph structures and ensure high-quality ingestion.
• Apply clustering, classification, anomaly detection, and other machine learning techniques to graph-structured data to enhance fraud detection capabilities.
• Design, implement, and optimize graph data pipelines, schemas, and data models that support high-complexity networks and large-scale analytic environments.
• Document methodologies, graph models, code, and analytic outputs in accordance with PRAC data governance, EDM standards, and federal oversight requirements.
• Collaborate with PRAC stakeholders, OIG partners, and law enforcement to refine analytic approaches, validate graph-based findings, and support cross-program risk identification.
• Conduct graph-based investigative analysis using open-source, law enforcement, and third-party data to support lead generation and case development.
• Build link analysis diagrams, entity relationship charts, and graph-based intelligence products that visualize complex networks and relationships across multiple data sources.
• Use graph analytics to validate PRAC-developed analytic rules and model outputs, performing due diligence to confirm or refute potential fraud indicators.
• Support OIG and law enforcement partners by producing customized investigative work products and presenting graph-derived insights in clear, actionable formats.
• Follow PRAC investigative workflows, templates, and policies for handling law-enforcement-sensitive data and multi-agency investigative information.
• Evaluate emerging graph analytics tools, graph databases, and data sources; provide recommendations aligned with PRAC mission needs and federal policy.
• Collaborate with PRAC's OCIO, OCISO, and OCDO to configure, integrate, and optimize approved graph tools within the PRAC analytic environment.
• Support ingestion of new data sources into graph environments, including schema design, transformation logic, and quality control.
• Assist PRAC in analyzing cutting-edge graph-based AI/ML tools and technologies, providing technical documentation and risk considerations to support Government procurement decisions.
• Maintain awareness of evolving fraud schemes, graph analytic techniques, and cross-program risks to inform future capability development.
• Work closely with data scientists, investigators, statisticians, and engineers to integrate graph analytics into broader fraud detection and investigative workflows.
• Communicate complex graph-based findings to senior PRAC leadership, OIG partners, and non-technical stakeholders in clear, accessible terms.
• Ensure analytic integrity, reproducibility, and compliance across all graph-related workstreams.
• Contribute to continuous improvement of analytic processes, data quality, and graph-based fraud detection methodologies.

Required Qualifications:
• Three (3) or more years of hands-on experience using Neo4j or similar graph databases, including fluency in Cypher or comparable graph query languages.
• Deep understanding of graph theory and network science, including network topology, centrality measures, community detection, and shortest-path algorithms.
• Three (3) or more years of hands-on experience applying statistical and machine learning techniques-such as clustering, classifiers, and anomaly detection-to graph-structured data.
• Three (3) or more years of experience applying graph methods to fraud detection, knowledge graph development, and identification of hidden relationships.
• Experience designing, implementing, and optimizing graph data pipelines, graph data models, and schemas supporting high-complexity networks.
• Strong Python programming skills, including use of standard machine learning libraries (e.g., Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-Learn, NetworkX).
• Strong oral and written communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications:
• Experience supporting fraud analytics, investigative support, or program integrity efforts within federal oversight environments (e.g., OIGs, PRAC, CIGIE, law enforcement).
• Experience integrating multi-agency or multiprogram datasets into graph environments to detect cross-program risks and complex fraud schemes.
• Experience producing graph-based investigative work products such as link analysis diagrams, entity relationship charts, and network visualizations.
• Experience developing or deploying AI/ML models applied to graph data.
• Experience supporting enterprise data management (EDM), data governance, and federal data quality standards.
• Familiarity with PRAC AI governance policies, OMB memoranda (M-25-22, M-25-21, M-26-04), and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework.
• Advanced certifications in data science, graph analytics, or fraud examination (e.g., CFE, Neo4j Certified Professional).

Required Education: Bachelor's degree (BA/BS) in Data Science, Computer Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related quantitative field.

Preferred Education: Master's degree (MS/MA) in Data Science, Analytics, Computer Science, Statistics, or a related discipline.
